newsitem.title: UK: LME zinc perks up in pre-market, copper steadier.
newsitem.headline: LME zinc perks up in pre-market, copper steadier.

text.p: Buoyant zinc flirted with new seven-year highs on Monday during pre-market trading, traders said.
Flagship three months copper was steadier after a strong close above $2,300 a tonne resistance on Friday and was helping lift aluminium.
"The other metals are in the shadow of zinc this morning," a trader said, adding that investment bank buying was leading the morning's activity.
"Zinc is at a very important level around $1,535 and if it goes above it we'll see some more short covering and buy stops triggered."
It was last indicated at $1,534/$1,537, up from Friday's kerb close of $1,524.
The market is technically overbought, with the 14-day RSI around 77, but traders said zinc had near-term scope to push higher if more speculative buying emerged.
Copper was firmer at $2,325/2,327 after closing at $2,316 on Friday, near the day's highs on end-week position squaring.
Chart-wise the market might try to fill the rest of a $2,308-$2,365 gap, technical analysts said.
The cash to threes backwardation was about $10 narrower at $125/$135, and traders said they expected the spread to contract further as tight dates dropped off.
Aluminium was also slightly firmer with producer short covering said to be a feature.
Prices were last at $1,613/1,616 versus $1,607.50, with next resistance expected at $1,620.
Lead firmed with zinc to $655, after ending at $648/$649 on Friday.
But tin maintained the sluggish tone it adopted last week, clocking in at $5,450/5,470 versus $5,460. Important support was seen at $5,420.
Nickel was little changed at $6,780/$6,800, up from $6,740, while alloy was marked slightly firmer with primarly aluminium at $1,451/1,460, from $1,442/$1,445.
